subject: POC capacity planning - reserved GPUs & autoscale (Acme AI)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + POC success criteria (Acme AI)

Hi Samir and Jenna —

Great to meet with you both earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery + proposed next steps for the POC capacity plan: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary workload: real-time support chat (avg session length 45 tokens, peak concurrent sessions ~1,200)
- Expected peak QPS for generation: ~200 qps for short responses, heavier during product launches (burst to ~500 qps)
- Latency SLO: 200ms p95 (user-facing)
- Success criteria: accuracy on the provided test prompts (≥92% match to baseline), sustained p95 latency ≤250ms under peak test load, and stable KV cache hit rate ≥35% during steady state

Proposed POC plan (high level):
1) Reserved GPUs for baseline: 4 x A100-80GB (to cover sustained throughput during working hours)
2) Autoscale policy: allow burst-to 8 GPUs (fast spin-up to handle traffic spikes) with 5-minute cooldown and pre-warmed spare instance during peak windows
3) Capabilities to test: latency under load, token cost/auditing, model variant fallback behavior, KV caching effectiveness
4) Timeline: prep (2 weeks), POC run (2 weeks), evaluation & decision (1 week) — target POC start: Sep 7, 2026
5) Ownership: Marissa (POC lead, Redwood) / Samir (POC lead, Acme AI) / Dylan (runtime config & infra) / Jenna (evaluation & success criteria)

Attached is an initial capacity estimate and a proposed MOA (scope & timelines). Please review and let me know adjustments — specifically if your burst expectations should be higher or if you want longer POC duration.

Next steps:
- Samir/Jenna: confirm success criteria and POC start date
- Redwood (Dylan/Aditya): confirm reserved GPU availability and autoscale warm pool approach
- I'll circulate an updated MOA and a short SLA for the trial once we confirm numbers

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

From: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jenna Reed <jenna.reed@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + POC success criteria (Acme AI)

Thanks Marissa — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Success criteria: agree on the accuracy threshold (we'll run the test prompt suite and provide a gold set). The 92% match is fine as a starting point — Jenna will detail the scoring rules.
- Peak/burst expectations: during marketing blasts we have seen short bursts that could approach 800 qps for 10-20 minutes (not sustained). Can Redwood's autoscale plan handle that without significant cold starts?
- Reserved capacity: we want to make sure baseline 4 x A100 covers concurrent steady traffic outside of bursts; if not, happy to adjust.
- Network checklist: our security team will want to validate egress and VPC requirements; can you share the network checklist and required IP ranges?

We can confirm a Sep 7 start provided the reserved capacity and warm pool behavior are acceptable. I'll also loop in our infra/security folks if needed.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, Acme AI
samir@acme.ai | +1 212-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jenna Reed <jenna.reed@acme.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + POC success criteria (Acme AI)

Thanks — good questions. Short answers below and a more detailed plan attached.

- Burst handling: Redwood supports warm pools and very fast spin-up (our autoscaler can bring an extra GPU online in ~60–90s when using pre-warmed containers; cold boot without warm pool is ~4–5 minutes). For the 10–20 minute 800 qps blasts you described, we recommend:
  * Maintain a warm pool of 2 GPUs during campaign windows (pre-warmed instances that are billed as part of reserved/burst allocation)
  * Autoscale up to 8 GPUs with progressive ramping: immediate warm pool + 4 GPUs within 90s + remaining up to 8 in 3–5 minutes.

- Baseline capacity: based on the workload profile in the attached spreadsheet we expect 4 x A100-80GB to cover steady-state ~200 qps with p95 ≈180–220ms assuming KV caching is effective. If you anticipate frequent higher baseline, we can increase reserved to 6 GPUs.

- Network checklist: attached network_checklist.docx with required IP ranges and VPC peering notes. Happy to run a brief tech session with your infra team next week.

Attached: detailed capacity estimate (spreadsheet) and updated MOA with warm-pool costing.

Proposed updated timeline:
- Aug 31: Confirm reserved GPU count + warm pool size + test prompt suite
- Sep 3–4: Provisioning & pre-warm setup (Redwood infra)
- Sep 7–20: POC execution window
- Sep 21–24: Evaluation & debrief

I'll also propose a short KPI dashboard we'll share daily during the run (p95 latency, tokens, cost, cache hit rate, error rate).

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: network_checklist.docx (DOCX, 18KB)

All set on our end — Jenna confirmed the scoring rubric and our infra team okayed the network checklist with a small comment on egress logging (we'll share details Tuesday). We're happy to proceed with the following:

- Reserved GPUs: 4 x A100-80GB baseline, with option to increase to 6 if live traffic requires it
- Warm pool: 2 pre-warmed GPUs during campaign windows
- Autoscale: up to 8 GPUs, priority ramping as described
- POC start: Sep 7, 2026 (provisioning Sep 3)
\Please send over the MOA and the short daily KPI dashboard template and we'll sign the MOA by end of day Wednesday.
\Thanks everyone — looking forward to it.
\Samir
